confirmed: The three handler schemas accept decimal-string tab_id and locally reject limit:0 or empty request_id as proposed. Tools Run validates locally then invokes handler.run with permissionMode=act and assignedTabId=null, bypassing dispatcher gates.

Console capture must be armed before the click. clear:false peeks; clear:true consumes the first limit records before filtering. The public Selenium fixture currently has #consoleLog calling console.log('Hello, world!').

Network capture must be armed before the document reload. read_network_requests consumes queued records even with clear:false and filters by URL afterward. The public Web form currently returns HTTP 200 text/html and contains the title marker.

get_request_body delegates to Network.getResponseBody and therefore reads the completed GET response body by request_id in the same live CDP session. Calling it a POST request-payload test would be false coverage.
A full extension Reload and fresh capture/request_id are correctly distinguished from a page reload; detach and worker restart can clear in-memory buffers.

findings.issue: The shared setup does not explicitly grant and verify Chrome's optional debugger permission in each disposable member/admin profile before positive Tools runs. The manual runner bypasses the dispatcher's optional-permission check, while the handlers still need debugger attach. An attach failure would otherwise be ambiguous and the proposed positive procedure may be blocked at its first step.
findings.correction: Add a setup step to enable Advanced agent capabilities in Settings through the user gesture and verify chrome.permissions.contains({permissions:['debugger']}) or an equivalent visible permission state in each profile; record a refusal as an environment/permission-gate outcome, never as a handler result. Do not use a programmatic grant shortcut.

findings.issue: The original three cases retain a permissions dimension, but the proposal only says that a separate dispatcher run should prove advertisement and choose Deny. It supplies no repeatable prompt, capture timing, expected denial result, or role-specific evidence path. The direct Tools runs cannot establish this dimension; all permissions cells must remain unresolved.
findings.correction: Integrate the three direct-manual paths as bounded source-grounded procedures only. Add separately executable dispatcher permission cases with an exact advertised call, captured pre-denial state, actual privileged card Deny action, expected structured denial and unchanged capture state; keep their results pending until run.

findings.issue: Requiring exactly one completed document record is a strict oracle and can fail if Chrome emits an additional same-URL record or the public server redirects while still delivering the page. Such a result needs classification before calling the handler defective.
findings.correction: Record every matching URL/status/method/request_id in the disposable tab, select the one completed final 200 document GET for 4117, and classify duplicates/redirects as fixture or browser behavior unless they contradict the observed page. Preserve the strict single-record expectation as a clean-pass criterion, not a generic product defect.

acceptance_boundary: The direct manual proposals can populate preconditions, steps and expected results for valid-input, invalid-input and reload design. They cannot mark member/admin runtime cells verified or close the permissions dimension. Preserve the original modes and dimensions, and leave actual execution to the admitted native-browser test.

methods: read-only HTTP GET of the two public fixture pages
